Test Description: Verify default reset values and masked read/write behavior of per-pin and group GPIO registers.
Remarks: Selected registers are explicitly skipped in write/read and reset-value checks; default input may read as 1 unless the pin is forced low, and forcing low can affect bit-level select causing mismatches.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Start the test case execution
2) Iterate over GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_39; for each register that is readable, read the value and mask off the least significant bit before comparison
3) Compare the masked read value with the documented reset value for that register; record a default-value failure if they differ
4) For each of six predefined 32-bit test patterns, set the current write data for the upcoming write phase
5) Iterate over all configured GPIO and group registers; for each register whose write is enabled, write the test pattern masked by the register’s write mask
6) Iterate over the same address set; for each register whose write and read are both enabled, read the value and apply the read mask
7) For each read, compute the expected value by combining the masked write data for writable bits with the preserved reset value for non-writable bits, then compare against the masked read value
8) Record a write/read failure if any comparison mismatches are observed
9) Report PASS if no failures were recorded; otherwise report FAIL
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS: All masked reads equal expected values for every addressed register across all test patterns and all reset-value comparisons match. FAIL: Any default-value mismatch or any masked read mismatch is observed.

Test Description: Verify negative-edge interrupt generation for GPIO pads 8–39 including per-pin enable, raw status handling, group status checks, and system interrupt clearing.
Remarks: Use a known output-mapped address to create falling edges; arm the wait before generating the edge to avoid race conditions; use bounded timeouts to avoid infinite waits.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance via LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1
2) Drive the external pad control address 0xA0243ffc to all ones to establish a known high level
3) For each of GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_39: configure input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and request raw interrupt clear; insert a short wait between configurations
4) For each bit position 0..31: pre-clear the corresponding raw interrupt in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1
5) For the same bit: enable only that interrupt in GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 and insert a short wait
6) Arm the pending-wait before generating the edge
7) Create a falling edge for that bit by first driving 0xA0243ffc to all ones and then driving it with only that bit cleared
8) Wait for the interrupt to be serviced with a bounded timeout, advancing to the next bit if the timeout elapses
9) In the interrupt handler: drive 0xA0243ffc back to all ones to restore the idle level
10) Read the per-pin register for the active GPIO and check that the input state reflects a low after the falling edge
11) Read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the group status shows the active bit set
12) Clear the per-pin raw status by writing a value that preserves input mode and requests interrupt clear
13) Clear the group raw status for the active bit via GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 and verify GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 reads as zero
14) Clear the system-level raw status in LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 for the selected instance and clear the GIC interrupt line
15) Repeat for all 32 bits and report the aggregated result via the test completion mechanism
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS: For each pin, the input state reads low after the falling edge, the group interrupt status asserts then clears to zero after servicing, and the system raw status is cleared; no timeout occurs. FAIL: Any timeout occurs, input state is not low, group status bit is not set for the active pin, group status does not clear, or system raw status remains set.

Test Description: Verify positive-edge interrupt generation for GPIO pads 8–39 with per-pin enable, group input-mode configuration, group status handling, and system interrupt clearing.
Remarks: Group IO control is used to place pads in input mode; the group interrupt is masked during service and re-enabled afterward; a bounded timeout prevents infinite waits.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance via LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1
2) For each of GP0_GPIO_8 through GP0_GPIO_39: enable positive-edge interrupt generation
3) Configure pads 8–39 to input mode via GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1 through GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4 and insert a short wait
4) Enable all per-pin interrupts in GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1
5) For each pin index 0..31: drive the external pad control address 0xA0243ffc low, arm the pending-wait, then drive it high to create a single rising edge
6) Wait for the interrupt with a bounded timeout; on timeout, record an error and stop further iterations
7) After each interrupt, optionally drive the pad control low to prepare for the next iteration and insert a short wait
8) In the interrupt handler: read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm a nonzero group status; mask group interrupts by clearing GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 to zero during service
9) Clear per-pin raw status by writing the clear request to each per-pin register for pads 8–39 and wait briefly
10) Read GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm the value is zero after clears
11) Clear the system-level raw status in LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 for the active instance and verify it is cleared by a subsequent read
12) Re-enable group interrupts by writing all ones to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clear the corresponding GIC interrupt line
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS: A nonzero group interrupt status is observed on entry to the handler, per-pin raw clears drive the group status to zero, the system raw status clears on write and readback, and all iterations complete without timeout. FAIL: Group status not asserted, group status not cleared after service, system raw status not cleared, or a timeout occurs.
